chunk_notes.verdict:
I read 8147-8606 myself and re-opened every Lean declaration the reader named. Its Lean reading of the hand-written files is accurate throughout - I re-checked local_nogo line by line (it really does derive only pA, pC, pF and the three nonvanishings na, nc, nf, never pB and never e_u, g_u, so the 'six amplitudes' gap at 8349 stands), Orbit62.MomentSystem.pos really concludes only six of fourteen positivities (8408 stands), Orbit34 really has only e1 = stdBasis 0 and e2 = stdBasis 1 so 'for all distinct i,j' stands, and no_code for orbits 32 and 34 really discharges the wt <= 2 side condition of offSumOn_eq_zero_of_hasDistance by decide, with SS.PauliString.wt the genuine Pauli weight. I also broadened 8563: all seven order-five orbit files (CodeOrbit33/34/35/37/38/39/40) route every off-diagonal row through offSumOn_eq_zero_of_hasDistance, so the section-wide weight-two claim is carried for the whole section, not just orbit 34.

Where the reader went wrong is exactly where the orientation note warned: it treated MainTheory/Generated/ as machine-generated proof shards and searched only SixQubit/ and the hand-written MainTheory files. Generated holds a per-row moment matrix and rank certificate (OrbitTableRank01..66) plus a semantics file (OrbitTableSemantics01..66) that converts rank into the affine dimension of the row's nonnegative moment polytope. That single family refutes three of its findings: orbit 32's '23x32 system of rank twenty-three' is active_moment_rank = 23 (gap -> covered); orbit 63's 'moment family is one-dimensional' is lp_affine_dimension = 1 from rank 15 on 16 columns (gap -> covered); orbit 62's 'moment solution is unique' is lp_affine_dimension = 0 from rank 14 on 14 columns (tracked/partial -> covered); and orbit 32's nullity 32-23 = 9 is lp_affine_dimension = 9, which makes the reader's reason at 8263 wrong even though the residual gap (injectivity, 'complete affine normal form') is real. In each case I confirmed the row is the right orbit by decoding the literal column words and matching them against the SixQubit fibre literals and against RowFacts/all_rows, rather than trusting the file number - necessary here, since paperOrbitId shows the key ordering is a permutation of the manuscript ordering (key 33 is paper orbit 39, not 34).

chunk_notes.summary: This chunk is the tail of the projective-order-five no-go section of supplementary.tex: six consecutive subsections closing moment orbits 40, 39, 35, 38, 37 and 33, one obstruction mechanism each (a two-edge Walsh separation; a five-incidence full-rank flip system; three full-rank flip systems chained through the polytope; a 2x4 permanent obstruction; a 3x3 star-and-permanent obstruction; and a six-block reflection on a zero-angle qubit). chunk_notes.coverage: The six no-go verdicts themselves are solidly carried: each subsection's closing sentence ('orbit N is impossible/excluded') has a matching SixQubit.OrbitN.no_go_of_moments and, more importantly, a SixQubit.OrbitN.no_code that removes the moment hypothesis and derives False from support, unit norms and SS.HasDistance ![c,d] 3 alone. Where the prose is weakest is in the intermediate machinery, and the pattern is consistent: Lean systematically takes a shorter, division-free route than the manuscript and therefore does not state the manuscript's intermediate objects. Three recurring shapes account for nearly all the gaps. (1) Determinant/full-rank claims: the manuscript justifies isolation by computing a character-matrix determinant (16 for orbit 39, -160 for orbit 35, 160 for orbit 33's C), and no Matrix.det for any of these exists anywhere in the repository -- Lean instead takes two dressings and half-sums out the single monomial it needs. The orbit-39 and orbit-33 instances are already flagged partial by the ledger at displaymath@8658 and @8953, but the orbit-35 one at line 8696 is pure prose and had no entry at all, which is the most substantive new finding here. (2) Fiber structure taken for granted: 'the top fiber is the bitwise complement' and 'exact moment reduction gives equality of complementary probabilities' are asserted for orbits 37 and 38 and stated nowhere; complement theorems of exactly this form exist for orbits 36 and 53-65 but not for these two, so this is a cheap fix rather than a deep hole. chunk_notes.verdict: A strong report; 24 of 27 assertions survive scrutiny unchanged, and its two best findings hold up under attack. chunk_notes.summary: This chunk is three consecutive no-go proofs in the six-qubit orbit catalogue: orbit 17 (subsec:m2-orbit17), orbit 20 (subsec:m2-orbit20) and orbit 12 (subsec:m2-orbit12), each a Proposition asserting the orbit admits no exact ((6,2,d>=3)) completion. chunk_notes.coverage: The endpoints are solidly certified and the middles are not, in a way that is consistent across all three orbits. SixQubit.Hafnian.no_go, SixQubit.Orbit17.no_go_of_moments, SixQubit.Orbit20.no_go_of_moments and SixQubit.Orbit12.no_go_of_moments each derive False from the full hypothesis bundle, and I read every one of them plus SixQubit/Hafnian.lean and SixQubit/Spinor.lean in full: nothing is left open at the top. But in every case the Lean takes a deliberately different interior route, and says so in its own module headers -- no vertex scalings, no phase ratios, no spans or unit vectors, no division. The consequence is that the paper's interior prose steps are systematically unformalized rather than formalized differently: the maximum-degree enumeration for orbit 17 (Delta <= 2 path-or-cycle, the Delta = 3 "same argument applies to w", the Delta = 4 rank-four claim), and for orbit 12 the pairing x_e = x_ebar, the identity x_e = y_e, and the whole "positivity forces b_e into L; the H = 1 block similarly forces a_e into M" step, whose H = 1 half is never even formed in Lean (only mask efA and the H = 0 diagonal entries appear). I marked these low severity because the top-level theorems do not depend on them, but each is a real proof obligation the manuscript discharges in a sentence. Two things deserve more attention than their severity suggests. First, line 11531 states the remaining goal as "a graph with no isolated vertex cannot support nonzero edge labels satisfying all equations", which is literally false -- the star K_{1,5} is a counterexample -- and the paper's own Delta = 5 branch must fall back on the degree equations to kill it; SixQubit.Hafnian.Sys has the correct hypothesis bundle, so this is a prose defect rather than a mathematical one, but a reader following the sentence would be misled. Second, the two "for exact reproducibility" paragraphs (lines 11492 and 11758) assert five specific ranks and minors of moment matrices, and the repository has no rank or minor formalization for orbits 17 or 20 at all -- the only such development is SixQubit.Orbit31.momentMatrix_rank for a different orbit. Three findings run the other way and are better than the ledger's per-display statuses suggest: the star contradiction at 11580-11584 is carried line for line by SixQubit.Hafnian.star, the "no isolated vertex" corollary at 11491 is carried at all six vertices by MomentSystem.normalForm plus Hafnian.iso, and the positive-block/positive-pair existence claims at 11730 and 11867 are exactly the rcases splits that close the two no_go_of_moments proofs.
chunk_notes.verdict:
The reader's work on the SixQubit hand-written layer is accurate - I re-read SixQubit/Hafnian.lean, Spinor.lean and Triangle.lean in full and the relevant blocks of Orbit17.lean, Orbit20.lean and Orbit12.lean, and every quoted `have`, every linear_combination coefficient, every rcases split and every field name it cites is really there. Its two sharpest findings survive: the star K_{1,5} counterexample showing line 11531 is false as literally written (I re-checked it - every four-set through the centre has a non-star factor in each monomial, every four-set avoiding it has all three monomials zero, so all fifteen hafnians hold on a graph with no isolated vertex, and only Hafnian.Sys's degree fields d0-d5 rule it out), and the systematic observation that the manuscript's interior route (vertex scalings, phase ratios lambda and rho, spans, unit vectors, division) is not the route Lean takes.

Its one large error is the one the task warned about: it searched only SixQubit/ and the hand-written MainTheory files and concluded the repository has no rank or minor formalization for orbits 17 or 20. MainTheory/Generated/ contains OrbitTableRank01-66, one integer rank certificate per orbit, and OrbitTableSemantics01-66 on top of them. OrbitTableRank17.active_moment_rank is `rank = 23` on a 23x32 matrix and OrbitTableRank20.active_moment_rank is `rank = 20` - the manuscript's two headline numbers, verbatim. I did not take the file index on faith: I decoded both column vectors and matched them against SixQubit.Orbit17.S0/S1 (weights {0,4} / {2,6}) and against av = ![1,1,1,2,2,2] with the manuscript's R = {000,011,101,110}, and I read MainTheory/FiniteMomentMatrix.lean to confirm the 23 rows are the two normalizations plus the 21 signed degree-<=2 moment rows, i.e. the same system as the orbits' own MomentSystem structures. I also computed the two exhibited maximal minors from the kernel-verified entries: -1024 for orbit 17 and -512 for orbit 20, matching the manuscript's 1024 and -512. So three of the reader's gap reasons (11483, 11492, 11758) were written on a bad search and are corrected; the residual gaps there are much narrower - the determinant values are never stated as theorems, and the orbit-20 augmented system (rank 29, minor -4096, three-dimensional solution) is formed nowhere at all.

Two covereds are inflated by the reader's own disclosed caveats and I have flipped them to gap: 11730 ('all eight amplitudes ... nonzero' where Lean derives three) and 11867 (a bottom-variable claim carried only in the mirrored top variables, via the unproved x_e = y_e). I left the three orbit-17 graph-theoretic gaps standing after a fresh search - Hafnian.lean has no graph object, no degree function, no connectivity and no maximum-degree split, and MainTheory's only vertex-scaling and hafnian-case machinery (Orbit7VertexScaling, Orbit7GraphCaseEquations) is over Fin 5 for a different orbit, so it does not carry the K_6 statements. I also left 11579 as tracked: the determinant -48 is prose rather than the display it is attached to, but the ledger entry for eq:o17-triangle-system reviews that determinant explicitly and records it as having no Lean counterpart, so nothing is hidden by the label. Of the two things the reader missed, neither is a hole; both are generality claims ('an arbitrary candidate', 'span the restricted characters') that deserved to be looked at and turn out to be fully instantiated.

chunk_notes.coverage: The results of this chunk are solidly certified; the proofs of this chunk are only partly the ones Lean runs. Every no-go conclusion here -- orbits 13, 14, 15, 24, the fourteen-orbit theorem, and the eleven-survivor corollary with its seven determined images -- has a top-level declaration I opened and read, and the two strongest meta-claims in the chunk survive scrutiny: the weight-at-most-two restriction is structural (SS.HasDistance 3 = Detects 2), and the no-genericity claim is structural too (Completion carries no interior or face hypothesis, so NoCompletion holds on every boundary face). The single most load-bearing "analogous" hand-off, orbit 13's X_5 system at line 12003, is genuinely discharged: CodeOrbit13 supplies all eight ef1 rows with decide-checked weights, not a gesture. The real finding is a structural one that a display-by-display ledger cannot see. The manuscript's parity-four toolkit (lem:parity4-moment, lem:parity4-connectivity, lem:parity4-edgeisolation, lem:connected-orthogonality) is fully and faithfully formalized in MainTheory/ParityFour*.lean and MainTheory/ConnectedOrthogonality.lean -- and it is never used. grep for consumers of edge_isolation, exists_line, frame_forms_ne and positiveGraph_connected turns up only Audit.lean's #print axioms lines and the PaperSupplementaryImages wrappers. SixQubit/Orbit14.lean, Orbit15.lean and Orbit24.lean import SixQubit.ParityFour instead -- a completely different mechanism (wedge identities total8, slice_zero, plucker, lagrange) that reaches a stronger conclusion without any connectivity argument at all: for orbit 14 and 15 it proves both slices have zero mass rather than picking a positive-mass block, and for orbit 24 it runs a Pluecker/Lagrange endgame. So each of the three "Lemma X gives edgewise orthogonality, this graph is connected by Lemma Y, Lemma Z now contradicts W" sentences is a gap, and with them the never-built bridge from any orbit's MomentSystem into the cross-polytope. These are medium, not high: the theorems are true and certified, but a reader auditing the manuscript's stated derivations against the Lean will not find them there. The remaining gaps are cosmetic in comparison -- three prose determinant values (-16, 4096 twice, and W_k W_k^T = 8 I_8) that no declaration computes because the development inverts the character sums by a transversal argument that needs less, plus two unformalized intermediate steps (the S/S^c complementation, the three-cube decomposition) whose conclusions are separately proved by other routes.
chunk_notes.verdict:
I upheld all 33 of the reader's classifications and add five assertions it did not report. I could not refute a single one of its eight gaps, and I could not demote a single one of its twelve covereds.

What I did to try. (1) Determinants: grep for 4096/Hadamard/det over MainTheory, SixQubit, SS turns up only BinaryDet*/BinaryBeta* (0-1 6x6 matrices for the beta bound) and unrelated Generated/Coarse shard constants. I also opened MainTheory/ParityFourMomentMatrix.lean, a file the reader never mentioned -- it is a 16x16 moment matrix with an explicit integer inverse (inverseZ * matrixZ = 16*1, `by decide`), not the 4x4 Hadamard or the 8x8 W_k, so the three determinant gaps (-16, 4096 twice, W_k W_k^T = 8 I_8) stand. MainTheory/ParityFourEdgeIsolation.lean's own docstring concedes the point: it says W_k W_k^T = 8 I is "stated as the inversion it is used for", and the nearest declaration, sum_character_mul, is the 16x16 relation, not the 8x8 one. (2) The bridge gaps (12234, 12243, 12389) are confirmed by the Lean's own prose: SixQubit/ParityFour.lean's header says "The paper argues through connectivity of the positive support. That is awkward to formalize... The route taken here is a uniform inequality that never mentions the support at all." MomentEquations/momentPolytope/feasible_iff_crosspolytope appear nowhere outside the MainTheory/ParityFour* files; exists_line and frame_forms_ne have no consumer outside their own file and Audit.lean:1192-1193. (3) I opened block_zero, cd_entry, exists_line, frame_forms_ne, edge_isolation, edgeMasks_eq/transversal, two_body_moment_zero, probability_nonnegative_iff, boundary_support_positive_iff, interior_probability_positive, positiveGraph_adj_iff_hamming_one, m2_fourteen_nogos, m2_current_status_full, Completion/NoCompletion and SS.HasDistance/Detects, and each carries what the reader said.

Three factual slips in the reader's write-up that do not change any classification, but that an auditor rereading it should not trust: (a) its 12000 entry says grep for "4096" "returns no hit" -- there are hits (FiveQubitCitedGateData.lean:176, several Generated/Coarse shards); all are irrelevant, so the gap is right for the wrong stated reason. (b) Its coverage note and several entries say edge_isolation / exists_line / frame_forms_ne are consumed by "the PaperSupplementaryImages wrappers" -- they are not; only parity4_moment (line 150) and parity4_connectivity (line 160) have wrappers, so the three isolation/orthogonality lemmas have strictly zero non-audit consumers. That strengthens the gaps. (c) Its 12047 entry calls block_zero's conclusion "Tr C_r = 0"; it is (C_r)_00 = 0. The classification survives because no_go_of_moments applies block_zero eight times -- four blocks x both free-bit halves -- which does cover both diagonal entries, and I checked the block indices decode to R = {000,011,101,110}. Its 12191 entry cites Audit.lean:1185 for exists_line; that line is edge_isolation_of_character_rows, exists_line is audited at 1192.

Two judgment calls I deliberately left alone. The 12093 gap (chi_S = -chi_S^c on O) is within two rfl-steps of stated lemmas: character_bxor_left plus parity_eq_bdot gives chi_{z xor allOnes}(x) = chi_z(x) * chi_allOnes(x), and chi_allOnes x = +/-1 by parity is definitional. But no declaration states it -- "character allOnes x = 1" exists only as an unnamed `have` at ParityFourEdgeIsolation.lean:172, and only for the even class -- so under the strict standard it is a gap, just the mildest kind. Symmetrically, the reader's 12156 covered (hamming_one_changes_parity + bxor_bxor_cancel) is assembled from pieces in the same way; I left it covered because hamming_one_changes_parity does state the mathematical content outright. Finally, 12421 ("Every proof uses only physical errors of weight at most two and is valid on all boundary faces") is correctly covered for its operative content -- HasDistance psi 3 unfolds to "for every P with P.wt <= 2" and Completion carries no face hypothesis -- but note the sentence is about the manuscript's fourteen proofs, and for orbits 14, 15 and 24 those are demonstrably not the proofs Lean runs, so what transfers is the property of the conclusions, not of the manuscript's arguments.

The reader's central structural finding is correct and is, in my view, the real output of this chunk: the manuscript's parity-four toolkit is fully formalized and entirely unused, and the three "edgewise orthogonality + connectivity + connected orthogonality" hand-offs are unformalized derivations of certified conclusions. I found a fourth instance of that hand-off (orbit 24, line 12311) and a fifth (orbit 14's slice-connectivity step, line 12385) that it did not report.
